module

public import Mathlib.Topology.Algebra.InfiniteSum.Group

@[expose] public section

open Filter
open scoped Topology

variable {ι α β : Type*} [CommGroup α] [TopologicalSpace α] [IsTopologicalGroup α]
  {f : β → α} {l : Filter ι} {s : ι → Set β}

@[to_additive]
lemma Multipliable.tendsto_tprod_one (hf : Multipliable f) (hs : ∀ b, ∀ᶠ i in l, b ∉ s i) :
    Tendsto (fun i ↦ ∏' b : s i, f b) l (𝓝 1) := by
  rw [tendsto_iff_eventually]
  rintro p hp
  obtain ⟨t, ht⟩ := hf.tprod_vanishing hp
  filter_upwards [t.eventually_all.2 fun b _ ↦ hs b] with i hi
  exact ht _ <| by simpa [Set.disjoint_right]

review.notes:
Reviewed Multipliable.tendsto_tprod_one and its generated twin Summable.tendsto_tsum_zero; the file introduces no definitions. Both correctly express vanishing of unconditional subproducts/subsums over sets that eventually omit every fixed index. The hypothesis is equivalent to eventual avoidance of each finite set, not to eventual emptiness for an infinite index type.

The assumptions agree with Mathlib's vanishing lemmas. Without completeness, some subfamilies may be nonsummable, but the statement consistently uses Mathlib's existing identity-valued defaults; it does not assert convergence of every subfamily. The sole library application, in HasFejerGaps.hasFabryGaps, uses real reciprocal series whose restricted tails are genuinely summable. No problem directly references either reviewed lemma, and no duplicate Mathlib declaration was found.

/workspace/review/scratch.lean compiled successfully. It checks the finite-avoidance equivalence, empty and finite index types, the trivial group, a bottom source filter, finite computations, geometric tails, moving singletons, and the actual reciprocal-tail application. Both reviewed lemmas depend only on propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound.
